AGENT PLAN
============

Title: Isolette English → GUMBO Contract Synthesis Plan (for SysML v2 models)
Authoring context: Use Appendix A of FAA REMH (pp. 92–A25/A26) as the normative English source; SysML v2 structural models are provided; this plan tells the agent how to produce GUMBO contracts and embed them in the SysML v2 files for Sireum/HAMR/Logika verification.

---
0) OBJECTIVE
------------
Given: SysML v2 element structure (threads/parts/ports) exists but lacks GUMBO contracts.
Goal: Convert English requirements from Appendix A into GUMBO contracts embedded in each SysML v2 element, using the exact “language "GUMBO"” pattern found in the repo, suitable for Sireum CLI parse + HAMR codegen + Logika proof.

Primary English sources and anchors (Appendix A):
- A.1–A.2: Overview and use/exception cases (pp. 92 onward).
- A.3: External entities & environmental assumptions (EA-*).
- A.4: Safety requirements (e.g., alarm <= 5 s).
- A.5.*: Functions (Regulate/Monitor + subfunctions): includes concrete “shall” statements.
  • A.5.1.1 Manage Regulator Interface (MRI): REQ-MRI-* (display rounding, interface failure, desired range mux).
  • A.5.1.2 Manage Regulator Mode (MRM): diagram A-4 (INIT/NORMAL/FAILED + 1.0 s timeout).
  • A.5.1.3 Manage Heat Source (MHS): REQ-MHS-1..5 + latency rationale (<= 6 s).
  • A.5.2.1 Manage Monitor Interface (MMI): REQ-MMI-1..7 (monitor status, interface failure, alarm range mux).
  • A.5.2.2 Manage Monitor Mode (MMM): diagram A-6 (INIT/NORMAL/FAILED + 1.0 s timeout).
  • A.5.2.3 Manage Alarm (MA): REQ-MA-1..5 + hysteresis bands and <= 5 s activation.

---
1) CONTRACT EMBEDDING: CANONICAL BLOCK
--------------------------------------
Embed one GUMBO block per SysML v2 element that implements the English functionality (MRI, MRM, MHS, MMI, MMM, MA, etc.). Use the exact structure and section order shown below.

SysML v2 snippet (inside the element body):

language "GUMBO" /*{
  state
    // (optional) persistent variables for previous outputs, timers, accumulators
    lastCmd: Isolette_Data_Model::On_Off;

  functions
    // (optional) pure helper definitions; must be side-effect-free
    def timeout_condition_satisfied(): Base_Types::Boolean := T;

  integration
    // Environmental assumptions (EA-* tables), port/data range constraints, cross-component invariants
    assume <IdOrTableLabel> "Short text | <deep-pdf-link#page=N>":
      <boolean_formula>;
    // …more assumes…

  initialize
    // Guarantees at initialize entrypoint (one-cycle init behavior)
    guarantee <name>: <boolean_formula>;

  compute
    // Per-dispatch (periodic) behavioral logic; one case per English “shall”
    compute_cases
      case <CaseId> "English paraphrase | <deep-pdf-link#page=N>":
        assume <guards>;
        guarantee <post-conditions>;
      // more case …
}*/

Formatting constraints:
- Keep the quoted English + the deep PDF link in each case/assume (for traceability).
- Use model namespaces (e.g., Isolette_Data_Model::Status.Init_Status) exactly as in the SysML files.
- Use Wstatus records consistently (e.g., lower_alarm_tempWstatus.degrees, .status).
- Keep boolean syntax: & (and), | (or), implies, == equality, and literal T/F or true false if they are T/F are not defined (as used in your repo).

---
2) WHEN TO USE EACH SECTION
---------------------------
2.1 state
- Add if the English requires memory:
  • Hysteresis “shall not be changed” / “hold previous” (Heat within desired band; Alarm no-change band).
  • Timeouts (duration in mode > 1.0 s) if not directly available from the platform as a primitive.
  Pattern examples:
    lastHeat: Isolette_Data_Model::On_Off
    initElapsed: Base_Types::S64  // time units per your modeling conventions

2.2 functions
- Add pure helper predicates for reusable logic, e.g.:
    def in_reset_band(t, lo, hi): Boolean := lo + 0.5[s32] <= t & t <= hi - 0.5[s32]

2.3 integration 
Guarantees: When to Use
-----------------------------------
Use **integration.guarantee** when your element is the **producer** of a property that:
- Must hold for **all time** (init + compute).
- Is **not** contingent on a transient case condition (e.g., mode or alarm band), and
- Is best treated as a cross-interface invariant (e.g., ordering, units, encoding domain).

- Place environmental assumptions (EA-*). Typical content:
  • Sensor temperature range/units/precision (A.3.2).
  • Isolette warm/cool slew limits ±1°F/min (A.3.1) – used to justify latency.
  • Operator Interface ranges and ordering of desired/alarm temps (A.3.4).
  Example:
    assume Table_A_12_LowerAlarmTemp "...|#page=112": 96 [s32] <= lower_alarm_tempWstatus.degrees & lower_alarm_tempWstatus.degrees <= 101 [s32];
    assume Table_A_12_UpperAlarmTemp "...|#page=112": 97 [s32] <= upper_alarm_tempWstatus.degrees & upper_alarm_tempWstatus.degrees <= 102 [s32];

  Example (MMI REQ-MMI-1): monitor_status == Isolette_Data_Model::Status.Init_Status.

2.5 compute / compute_cases
compute 
- You may add assume/guarantees if they the English suggests they hold for all of the below compute_cases.
Compute_cases
- Create one case per “shall”. Each case:
  • “assume” = guard from the English (mode, value status, inequality).
  • “guarantee” = post-condition effect on outputs/state.
- Use English paraphrase + deep link in case title.

    compute_cases

      case REQ_MMI_7 "If interface failure True ⇒ UNSPECIFIED |<pdf#page=113>":

}*/

# Small Drone Lifecycle Governor

## Selected system context

### Synopsis, need, purpose, and goals

NEED-01: A configurable unmanned drone needs one bounded logical authority that turns
finite lifecycle requests and a qualitative battery report into a coherent commanded
lifecycle phase, lifecycle-enablement outcome, and pilot-visible attention status. The
modeled concern is command governance, not proof that the drone physically achieves a
requested condition.

PURPOSE-01: The Small Drone Lifecycle Governor will govern the source-named `Off`,
`Standby`, `Charging`, `Ready`, and `Flying` lifecycle vocabulary for one logical drone
boundary. It will admit only explicitly permitted transitions, use qualitative battery
awareness when charging or flight readiness is requested, place the commanded lifecycle
in `Off` after invalid input, and require neutral observation followed by a fresh
request before operation resumes.

GOAL-01: The system shall publish one unambiguous commanded phase and mutually coherent
power, charging, and flight permissions for every finite input and state combination.

GOAL-02: The system shall distinguish valid low-battery awareness from invalid input and
shall expose the distinction to the monitoring pilot without claiming physical battery
performance.

GOAL-03: The system shall prevent an invalid or previously sampled request from being
replayed as an operational transition during recovery.

GOAL-04: The system should remain small enough for complete case enumeration,
responsibility audit, trace review, and human review without count-only usages or
interactions.

### Operational context and exact system boundary

CTX-01: The Lifecycle Request Source is outside the system and supplies one request
event plus its validity status per logical evaluation. The corpus does not name this
source; introducing it is an explicit pilot abstraction and does not assign command
authority to the pilot.

CTX-02: The Battery Management Context is outside the system and supplies a qualitative
capacity indication plus validity status. The abstract neither measures charge nor
infers physical endurance.

CTX-03: The Drone Lifecycle Enactor is outside the system and receives a logical
enablement outcome. Receipt is observable at the boundary; physical execution or success
is outside scope.

CTX-04: The Pilot is outside the system and receives commanded-phase and attention
reports for monitoring. The source supports the pilot's monitoring role only; no pilot
command role is inferred.

MON-01: `LifecycleRequestSample` is a finite root input from CTX-01 with fields `event :
LifecycleEvent` and `status : InputStatus`. `LifecycleEvent` is exactly `{NoRequest,
SwitchOn, SwitchOff, BeginCharge, EndCharge, Activate, Deactivate, BeginFlight,
EndFlight}` and `InputStatus` is exactly `{Valid, Invalid}`.

MON-02: `BatterySample` is a finite root input from CTX-02 with fields `indication :
BatteryIndication` and `status : InputStatus`. `BatteryIndication` is exactly
`{Adequate, Low}`; these labels are qualitative pilot abstractions with no numeric
charge, endurance, or unit claim.

CTRL-01: `LifecycleActuation` is a finite root output to CTX-03 with fields `power :
PowerPermission`, `chargingPermitted : Boolean`, and `flightPermitted : Boolean`.
`PowerPermission` is exactly `{Disabled, StandbyEnabled, OperationalEnabled}`. These are
commanded logical permissions, not achieved physical states.

CTRL-02: `CommandedPhaseReport` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly the
`LifecyclePhase` values `{Off, Standby, Charging, Ready, Flying}` and reports the phase
selected for the completed evaluation.

CTRL-03: `AttentionStatus` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly `{None, LowBattery,
InputFault, RecoveryAwaitingNeutral}`. It reports the highest-priority current attention
condition and does not assert a physical hazard classification.

### Nominal, boundary, fault, and recovery behavior

RISK-01: If an invalid request or battery report were treated as trustworthy, the
governor could publish an unintended lifecycle permission. The consequence within this
logical model is an incoherent or unjustified command, not an asserted physical accident
or severity classification.

### Essential environmental assumptions and constraints

ASM-01: CTX-01 is responsible for presenting exactly one event/status pair per logical
evaluation and for presenting `NoRequest` when no event is requested. This assumption is
needed to define neutral recovery; it does not claim how an external sender detects
edges or schedules samples.

ASM-02: CTX-02 is responsible for pairing every qualitative indication with an explicit
validity status. `Adequate` and `Low` are mutually exclusive finite labels supplied to
the governor; the abstract does not define a numeric boundary or guarantee their
physical accuracy.

ASM-03: CTX-03 is responsible only for accepting CTRL-01 as a logical command interface.
The governor receives no achievement feedback, so commanded phase shall never be
described as achieved flight, completed charging, landing, or physical power state.

ASM-04: CTX-04 is responsible only for receiving CTRL-02 and CTRL-03. Monitoring does
not imply that the pilot originated requests or that any external actor acted on the
report.

## Supporting contract definitions

### State `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Decision_Owner::current_phase`

State `current_phase` has type `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Phase`.

### State `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Decision_Owner::recovery_required`

State `recovery_required` has type `Base_Types::Boolean`.

## Detailed behavioral requirements

### Requirements for Attention Derivation

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the initialization phase

##### `INITIAL_ATTENTION_NONE` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the initialization phase, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to None.

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the compute phase

##### `ATTENTION_INPUT_FAULT` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when T is true, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Input Fault.

##### `ATTENTION_RECOVERY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when F is true and decision disposition recovery pending is true exactly when T is true, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Recovery Awaiting Neutral.

##### `ATTENTION_LOW_BATTERY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when F is true, decision disposition recovery pending is true exactly when F is true, and battery assessment is Low Battery, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Low Battery.

##### `ATTENTION_NONE` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when F is true, decision disposition recovery pending is true exactly when F is true, and battery assessment is not Low Battery, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to None.

### Requirements for Battery Assessment

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the initialization phase

##### `SAFE_INITIAL_BATTERY_FACT` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the initialization phase, Battery Assessment shall set battery assessment to Invalid Battery.

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the compute phase

##### `BATTERY_INVALID` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if raw battery status is Invalid, Battery Assessment shall set battery assessment to Invalid Battery.

##### `BATTERY_ADEQUATE` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if raw battery status is Valid and raw battery indication is Adequate, Battery Assessment shall set battery assessment to Adequate Battery.

##### `BATTERY_LOW` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if raw battery status is Valid and raw battery indication is Low, Battery Assessment shall set battery assessment to Low Battery.

### Requirements for Controlled Outcome Derivation

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the initialization phase

##### `INITIAL_ACTUATION_DISABLED` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the initialization phase, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Disabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when F is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when F is true.

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the compute phase

##### `ACTUATION_OFF` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if selected phase is Off, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Disabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when F is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when F is true.

##### `ACTUATION_STANDBY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if selected phase is Standby, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Standby Enabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when F is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when F is true.

##### `ACTUATION_CHARGING` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if selected phase is Charging, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Operational Enabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when T is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when F is true.

##### `ACTUATION_READY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if selected phase is Ready, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Operational Enabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when F is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when F is true.

##### `ACTUATION_FLYING` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if selected phase is Flying, Controlled Outcome Derivation shall set lifecycle actuation power to Operational Enabled, lifecycle actuation charging permitted to true exactly when F is true, and lifecycle actuation flight permitted to true exactly when T is true.

### Requirements for Lifecycle Decision Owner

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the initialization phase

##### `INITIAL_OWNER_STATE_AND_OUTPUTS` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the initialization phase, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the compute phase

##### `RECOVERY_IMPLIES_OFF` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall produce a result for which if recovery required is true, then current phase is Off, selected phase is current phase, and phase report is selected phase.

##### `CASE_01_INVALID_INPUT` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is Invalid Request or battery assessment is Invalid Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when T is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when T is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when T is true.

##### `CASE_02_RECOVERY_BLOCKS_REPLAY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when T is true, and qualified request is not No Request, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when T is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when T is true.

##### `CASE_03_NEUTRAL_CLEARS_RECOVERY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when T is true, and qualified request is No Request, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_04_SWITCH_OFF` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, and qualified request is Switch Off, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_05_SWITCH_ON` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Off, and qualified request is Switch On, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Standby, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Standby, phase report to Standby, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_06_BEGIN_CHARGE` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Standby, qualified request is Begin Charge, and battery assessment is Low Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Charging, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Charging, phase report to Charging, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_07_END_CHARGE` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Charging, qualified request is End Charge, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Standby, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Standby, phase report to Standby, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_08_ACTIVATE` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Standby, qualified request is Activate, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Ready, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Ready, phase report to Ready, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_09_BEGIN_FLIGHT` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Ready, qualified request is Begin Flight, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Flying, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Flying, phase report to Flying, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

##### `CASE_11_DEACTIVATE` — Conditional behavior

##### `CASE_12_HOLD` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, qualified request is not Switch Off, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Off and qualified request is Switch On, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Standby, qualified request is Begin Charge, and battery assessment is Low Battery, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Charging, qualified request is End Charge, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Standby, qualified request is Activate, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Ready, qualified request is Begin Flight, and battery assessment is Adequate Battery, it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Flying and qualified request is End Flight, and it is not the case that the value of current phase on entry is Ready and qualified request is Deactivate, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall preserve the value of current phase on entry, set recovery required to true exactly when F is true, set selected phase to the value of current phase on entry, set phase report to the value of current phase on entry, set decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and set decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create a codegen-only periodic projection of one candidate SysML model.

This helper deliberately accepts one explicit model path.  It never searches a
dataset tree and rejects evaluator/oracle paths, so staging cannot expose an
answer model to an application agent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path


THREAD = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)part\s+def\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s+:>\s+(?:AADL::)?Thread\s*\{[ \t]*$"
)
GUMBO_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r'(?P<open>language\s+"GUMBO"\s*/\*\{)(?P<body>.*?)(?P<close>\}\*/)',
    re.DOTALL,
)
GUMBO_INITIALIZE = re.compile(
    r"(?ms)^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)initialize[ \t]*(?:\r?\n)"
    r".*?(?=^(?P=indent)(?:compute|functions|invariants|integration|state)\b|\Z)"
)
PACKAGE = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*package\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\{")
SYSTEM_DEF = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^\s*part\s+def\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+:>\s+(?:AADL::)?System\s*\{"
)
PART_USE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^(?P<indent>[ \t]*)part\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*:\s*"
    r"(?P<target>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*;"
)


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def portable_path(path: Path) -> str:
    return Path(os.path.relpath(path.resolve(), Path.cwd().resolve())).as_posix()


def reject_contaminating_path(path: Path) -> None:
    lowered = {part.lower() for part in path.parts}
    if "evaluator" in lowered or path.name.lower() == "oracle.sysml":
        raise SystemExit("refusing evaluator/oracle model path")


def _blank_preserving_lines(value: str) -> str:
    """Erase source text while retaining exact line and column positions."""
    return "".join(character if character in "\r\n" else " " for character in value)


def strip_gumbo_initialization_sections(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Remove initialization contracts from the non-normative codegen view.

    HAMR initialization APIs do not expose input ports.  Consequently, an
    otherwise valid model-level ``initialize`` guarantee that refers to an
    input generates uncompilable Slang (both Initialization_Api and PostState
    containers lack that member).  Selectively rewriting expressions would
    invent semantics, so the executable projection consistently removes the
    complete initialization section from every GUMBO block.  The original
    candidate is checked by model Logika before this projection is created.

    Whitespace replacement preserves line numbers for diagnostics and leaves
    state, functions, invariants, integration, and compute sections verbatim.
    """
    removed = 0

    def project_block(block_match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        nonlocal removed
        body = block_match.group("body")

        def remove_section(section_match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
            nonlocal removed
            removed += 1
            return _blank_preserving_lines(section_match.group(0))

        projected_body = GUMBO_INITIALIZE.sub(remove_section, body)
        return block_match.group("open") + projected_body + block_match.group("close")

    return GUMBO_BLOCK.sub(project_block, text), removed


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("source", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("metadata", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--period-ms", type=int, default=1000)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    source = args.source.resolve()
    destination = args.destination.resolve()
    metadata = args.metadata.resolve()
    reject_contaminating_path(source)
    if args.period_ms <= 0:
        raise SystemExit("--period-ms must be positive")

    original = source.read_bytes()
    text = original.decode("utf-8")
    packages = PACKAGE.findall(text)
    if len(packages) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"expected exactly one package, found {packages}")
    system_defs = set(SYSTEM_DEF.findall(text))
    system_uses = [
        (len(match.group("indent").expandtabs()), match.group("target"))
        for match in PART_USE.finditer(text)
        if match.group("target") in system_defs
    ]
    shallowest = min((depth for depth, _ in system_uses), default=-1)
    roots = [target for depth, target in system_uses if depth == shallowest]
    if len(roots) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            "expected exactly one root part usage targeting a System definition, "
            f"found {roots}"
        )
    if re.search(r"\bDispatch_Protocol\b|attribute\s+:>>\s+Period\b", text):
        raise SystemExit(
            "candidate already contains dispatch/period refinements; refusing to "
            "guess how to normalize them"
        )

    count = 0

    def add_periodic(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        indent = match.group("indent") + "  "
        return (
            match.group(0)
            + "\n"
            + indent
            + "attribute :>> Dispatch_Protocol = Periodic;\n"
            + indent
            + f"attribute :>> Period = {args.period_ms} [ms];"
        )

    projected = THREAD.sub(add_periodic, text)
    if count == 0:
        raise SystemExit("candidate contains no Thread definitions")
    if projected.count("attribute :>> Dispatch_Protocol = Periodic;") != count:
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: dispatch count does not match Threads")
    if projected.count(f"attribute :>> Period = {args.period_ms} [ms];") != count:
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: period count does not match Threads")
    periodic_projection = projected
    projected, initialization_sections_removed = strip_gumbo_initialization_sections(
        periodic_projection
    )
    if projected.count("\n") != periodic_projection.count("\n"):
        raise SystemExit("internal projection error: initialization removal changed line count")
    remaining_initialization_headers = sum(
        len(re.findall(r"(?m)^[ \t]*initialize[ \t]*$", match.group("body")))
        for match in GUMBO_BLOCK.finditer(projected)
    )
    if remaining_initialization_headers:
        raise SystemExit(
            "unsupported GUMBO initialization layout remained after codegen projection"
        )

    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    metadata.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    destination.write_text(projected, encoding="utf-8")
    result = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "source": portable_path(source),
        "source_sha256": sha256(original),
        "projection": portable_path(destination),
        "projection_sha256": sha256(projected.encode("utf-8")),
        "package": packages[0],
        "system_definition": roots[0],
        "system_name": f"{packages[0]}::{roots[0]}",
        "thread_count": count,
        "period_ms": args.period_ms,
        "initialization_projection": "removed_from_codegen_view",
        "initialization_sections_removed": initialization_sections_removed,
    }
    metadata.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(result))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gate the original model, then create an isolated executable/codegen projection.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <agent/M-star.sysml> <new-work-directory> [external/sysml-aadl-libraries]" >&2
  exit 2
}

[[ $# -ge 2 && $# -le 3 ]] || usage

script_dir=$(realpath "$(dirname "$0")")
repo_root=$(realpath "$script_dir/..")
model=$(realpath "$1")
work_arg=$2
library=$(realpath "${3:-$repo_root/external/sysml-aadl-libraries}")

lower_model=${model,,}
case "/$lower_model/" in
  */evaluator/*|*/oracle.sysml/) echo "refusing evaluator/oracle model path" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[[ -f $model && $model == *.sysml ]] || { echo "candidate model not found: $model" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -d $library ]] || { echo "SysML AADL library not found: $library" >&2; exit 2; }
requirements="$(dirname "$model")/N.md"
[[ -f $requirements ]] || { echo "candidate requirements not found beside model: $requirements" >&2; exit 2; }

if [[ -e $work_arg ]]; then
  work=$(realpath "$work_arg")
  if find "$work" -mindepth 1 -print -quit | grep -q .; then
    echo "work directory must be new or empty: $work" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
else
  mkdir -p "$work_arg"
  work=$(realpath "$work_arg")
fi

if [[ -n ${SIREUM_BIN:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_BIN")
elif [[ -n ${SIREUM_HOME:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_HOME/bin/sireum")
else
  sireum=$(command -v sireum || true)
fi
[[ -n $sireum && -x $sireum ]] || {
  echo "Sireum executable not found; set SIREUM_BIN or SIREUM_HOME" >&2
  exit 2
}

mkdir -p "$work/evidence" "$work/staged" "$work/hamr"
cp "$requirements" "$work/N.md"
if [[ -f "$(dirname "$model")/.poolside/settings.local.yaml" ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$work/.poolside"
  cp "$(dirname "$model")/.poolside/settings.local.yaml" "$work/.poolside/settings.local.yaml"
fi
source_hash_before=$(sha256sum "$model" | awk '{print $1}')

# Acceptance gate 1 is intentionally run against the original candidate, not
# the executable projection. Keep the invocation identical to the campaign's
# named `sireum hamr sysml logika` gate.
set +e
"$sireum" hamr sysml logika \
  --sourcepath "$library" \
  "$model" >"$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log" 2>&1
integration_rc=$?
set -e
cat "$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log"
if [[ $integration_rc -ne 0 ]] || \
   grep -Eqi 'Resolution error:|Compilation failed|(^|[[:space:]])error:' "$work/evidence/original-model-logika.log"; then
  echo "ORIGINAL_MODEL_LOGIKA_FAILED rc=$integration_rc" >&2
  exit 1
fi

projection="$work/staged/M-star.executable.sysml"
metadata="$work/staged/projection.json"
python3 "$script_dir/stage_executable_model.py" \
  "$model" "$projection" "$metadata" >"$work/evidence/projection.jsonl"

package=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["package"])' "$metadata")
system_name=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["system_name"])' "$metadata")
slang_package=$(printf '%s' "$package" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

set +e
"$sireum" hamr sysml codegen \
  --platform JVM \
  --runtime-monitoring \
  --package-name "$slang_package" \
  --output-dir "$work/hamr" \
  --slang-output-dir "$work/hamr/slang" \
  --no-proyek-ive \
  --workspace-root-dir "$work/staged" \
  --sourcepath "$work/staged:$library" \
  --system-name "$system_name" \
  "$projection" >"$work/evidence/codegen.log" 2>&1
codegen_rc=$?
set -e
cat "$work/evidence/codegen.log"
if [[ $codegen_rc -ne 0 ]] || grep -Eqi 'Resolution error:|Compilation failed|(^|[[:space:]])error:' "$work/evidence/codegen.log"; then
  echo "EXECUTABLE_CODEGEN_FAILED rc=$codegen_rc" >&2
  exit 1
fi

slang="$work/hamr/slang"
component_root="$slang/src/main/component"
[[ -f $slang/bin/project.cmd ]] || { echo "codegen produced no Proyek project" >&2; exit 1; }
mapfile -d '' components < <(find "$component_root" -type f -name '*.scala' -print0 | sort -z)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Acceptance gate 2: prove both application entrypoints in every HAMR component.
set -euo pipefail

if [[ $# -lt 1 || $# -gt 2 ]]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <hamr-slang-root> [proof-output-directory]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

slang=$(realpath "$1")
proof_arg=${2:-$slang/proof}
mkdir -p "$proof_arg"
proof=$(realpath "$proof_arg")
work=$(realpath "$slang/../..")
component_root="$slang/src/main/component"
manifest="$work/generated-nonapplication.sha256"
allowlist="$work/generated-component-files.txt"
work_manifest="$work/protected-work-files.sha256"

[[ -d $component_root ]] || { echo "component root not found: $component_root" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f $manifest && -f $allowlist && -f $work_manifest ]] || {
  echo "prepared phase manifests are missing" >&2; exit 2;
}

if [[ -n ${SIREUM_BIN:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_BIN")
elif [[ -n ${SIREUM_HOME:-} ]]; then
  sireum=$(realpath "$SIREUM_HOME/bin/sireum")
else
  sireum=$(command -v sireum || true)
fi
[[ -n $sireum && -x $sireum ]] || {
  echo "Sireum executable not found; set SIREUM_BIN or SIREUM_HOME" >&2
  exit 2
}

# Fail closed if the application phase changed any generated non-application
# file or added/deleted a component application file.
if ! (cd "$slang" && sha256sum --check --quiet "$manifest"); then
  echo "generated non-application files changed after codegen" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! (cd "$work" && sha256sum --check --quiet "$work_manifest"); then
  echo "protected application-phase inputs changed after preparation" >&2
  exit 1
fi
current=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$current"' EXIT
(
  cd "$slang"
  find src/main/component -type f -name '*.scala' -print | sort
) >"$current"
if ! cmp -s "$allowlist" "$current"; then
  echo "component application file set differs from the generated allowlist" >&2
  diff -u "$allowlist" "$current" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

mapfile -t relative_components <"$allowlist"
[[ ${#relative_components[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "no generated components found" >&2; exit 1; }

method_timeout=${LOGIKA_METHOD_TIMEOUT:-30}
process_timeout=${LOGIKA_PROCESS_TIMEOUT:-180}
rlimit=${LOGIKA_RLIMIT:-2000000}
index=0
failures=0

for relative in "${relative_components[@]}"; do
  component="$slang/$relative"
  for method in initialise timeTriggered; do
    mapfile -t lines < <(
      awk -v method="$method" '
        $0 ~ ("^[[:space:]]*def[[:space:]]+" method "[[:space:]]*\\(") { print NR }
      ' "$component"
    )
    if [[ ${#lines[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
      echo "$relative must contain exactly one $method method; found ${#lines[@]}" >&2
      failures=$((failures + 1))
      continue
    fi
    safe_name=$(printf '%s-%s' "${relative%.scala}" "$method" | tr '/ ' '__')
    log=$(printf '%s/%03d-%s.log' "$proof" "$index" "$safe_name")
    index=$((index + 1))
    command=(
      "$sireum" proyek logika
      --timeout "$method_timeout"
      --rlimit "$rlimit"
      --par
      --line "${lines[0]}"
      "$slang"
      "$component"
    )
    printf 'PROVING %s:%s line=%s\n' "$relative" "$method" "${lines[0]}"
    set +e
    timeout "$process_timeout" "${command[@]}" >"$log" 2>&1
    rc=$?
    set -e
    cat "$log"
    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || \
       grep -Eqi 'Resolution error:|Compilation failed|RUN ABORTED|(^|[[:space:]])error:|\*\*\* Failed \*\*\*' "$log"; then
      echo "LOGIKA_FAILED component=$relative method=$method rc=$rc" >&2
      failures=$((failures + 1))
    else
      echo "LOGIKA_PASSED component=$relative method=$method"
    fi
  done
done

if [[ $failures -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "APPLICATION_LOGIKA_FAILED failures=$failures methods_attempted=$index" >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf 'APPLICATION_LOGIKA_PASSED components=%s methods=%s\n' \
  "${#relative_components[@]}" "$index"

# Small Drone Lifecycle Governor

## Selected system context

### Synopsis, need, purpose, and goals

NEED-01: A configurable unmanned drone needs one bounded logical authority that turns
finite lifecycle requests and a qualitative battery report into a coherent commanded
lifecycle phase, lifecycle-enablement outcome, and pilot-visible attention status. The
modeled concern is command governance, not proof that the drone physically achieves a
requested condition.

PURPOSE-01: The Small Drone Lifecycle Governor will govern the source-named `Off`,
`Standby`, `Charging`, `Ready`, and `Flying` lifecycle vocabulary for one logical drone
boundary. It will admit only explicitly permitted transitions, use qualitative battery
awareness when charging or flight readiness is requested, place the commanded lifecycle
in `Off` after invalid input, and require neutral observation followed by a fresh
request before operation resumes.

GOAL-01: The system shall publish one unambiguous commanded phase and mutually coherent
power, charging, and flight permissions for every finite input and state combination.

GOAL-02: The system shall distinguish valid low-battery awareness from invalid input and
shall expose the distinction to the monitoring pilot without claiming physical battery
performance.

GOAL-03: The system shall prevent an invalid or previously sampled request from being
replayed as an operational transition during recovery.

GOAL-04: The system should remain small enough for complete case enumeration,
responsibility audit, trace review, and human review without count-only usages or
interactions.

### Operational context and exact system boundary

CTX-01: The Lifecycle Request Source is outside the system and supplies one request
event plus its validity status per logical evaluation. The corpus does not name this
source; introducing it is an explicit pilot abstraction and does not assign command
authority to the pilot.

CTX-02: The Battery Management Context is outside the system and supplies a qualitative
capacity indication plus validity status. The abstract neither measures charge nor
infers physical endurance.

CTX-03: The Drone Lifecycle Enactor is outside the system and receives a logical
enablement outcome. Receipt is observable at the boundary; physical execution or success
is outside scope.

CTX-04: The Pilot is outside the system and receives commanded-phase and attention
reports for monitoring. The source supports the pilot's monitoring role only; no pilot
command role is inferred.

MON-01: `LifecycleRequestSample` is a finite root input from CTX-01 with fields `event :
LifecycleEvent` and `status : InputStatus`. `LifecycleEvent` is exactly `{NoRequest,
SwitchOn, SwitchOff, BeginCharge, EndCharge, Activate, Deactivate, BeginFlight,
EndFlight}` and `InputStatus` is exactly `{Valid, Invalid}`.

MON-02: `BatterySample` is a finite root input from CTX-02 with fields `indication :
BatteryIndication` and `status : InputStatus`. `BatteryIndication` is exactly
`{Adequate, Low}`; these labels are qualitative pilot abstractions with no numeric
charge, endurance, or unit claim.

CTRL-01: `LifecycleActuation` is a finite root output to CTX-03 with fields `power :
PowerPermission`, `chargingPermitted : Boolean`, and `flightPermitted : Boolean`.
`PowerPermission` is exactly `{Disabled, StandbyEnabled, OperationalEnabled}`. These are
commanded logical permissions, not achieved physical states.

CTRL-02: `CommandedPhaseReport` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly the
`LifecyclePhase` values `{Off, Standby, Charging, Ready, Flying}` and reports the phase
selected for the completed evaluation.

CTRL-03: `AttentionStatus` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly `{None, LowBattery,
InputFault, RecoveryAwaitingNeutral}`. It reports the highest-priority current attention
condition and does not assert a physical hazard classification.

### Nominal, boundary, fault, and recovery behavior

RISK-01: If an invalid request or battery report were treated as trustworthy, the
governor could publish an unintended lifecycle permission. The consequence within this
logical model is an incoherent or unjustified command, not an asserted physical accident
or severity classification.

### Essential environmental assumptions and constraints

ASM-01: CTX-01 is responsible for presenting exactly one event/status pair per logical
evaluation and for presenting `NoRequest` when no event is requested. This assumption is
needed to define neutral recovery; it does not claim how an external sender detects
edges or schedules samples.

ASM-02: CTX-02 is responsible for pairing every qualitative indication with an explicit
validity status. `Adequate` and `Low` are mutually exclusive finite labels supplied to
the governor; the abstract does not define a numeric boundary or guarantee their
physical accuracy.

ASM-03: CTX-03 is responsible only for accepting CTRL-01 as a logical command interface.
The governor receives no achievement feedback, so commanded phase shall never be
described as achieved flight, completed charging, landing, or physical power state.

ASM-04: CTX-04 is responsible only for receiving CTRL-02 and CTRL-03. Monitoring does
not imply that the pilot originated requests or that any external actor acted on the
report.

## Supporting contract definitions

### State `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Decision_Owner::current_phase`

State `current_phase` has type `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Phase`.

### State `Drone_Lifecycle_Governor::Lifecycle_Decision_Owner::recovery_required`

State `recovery_required` has type `Base_Types::Boolean`.

## Detailed behavioral requirements

### Requirements for Attention Derivation

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the initialization phase

##### `INITIAL_ATTENTION_NONE` — Required behavior

> During contract evaluation for the initialization phase, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to None.

#### Contract clauses evaluated in the compute phase

##### `ATTENTION_INPUT_FAULT` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when T is true, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Input Fault.

##### `ATTENTION_RECOVERY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when F is true and decision disposition recovery pending is true exactly when T is true, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Recovery Awaiting Neutral.

##### `ATTENTION_LOW_BATTERY` — Conditional behavior

> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if decision disposition input fault detected is true exactly when F is true, decision disposition recovery pending is true exactly when F is true, and battery assessment is Low Battery, Attention Derivation shall set attention status to Low Battery.

##### `ATTENTION_NONE` — Conditional behavior

1	# Small Drone Lifecycle Governor
     2	
     3	## Selected system context
     4	
     5	### Synopsis, need, purpose, and goals
     6	
     7	NEED-01: A configurable unmanned drone needs one bounded logical authority that turns
     8	finite lifecycle requests and a qualitative battery report into a coherent commanded
     9	lifecycle phase, lifecycle-enablement outcome, and pilot-visible attention status. The
    10	modeled concern is command governance, not proof that the drone physically achieves a
    11	requested condition.
    12	
    13	PURPOSE-01: The Small Drone Lifecycle Governor will govern the source-named `Off`,
    14	`Standby`, `Charging`, `Ready`, and `Flying` lifecycle vocabulary for one logical drone
    15	boundary. It will admit only explicitly permitted transitions, use qualitative battery
    16	awareness when charging or flight readiness is requested, place the commanded lifecycle
    17	in `Off` after invalid input, and require neutral observation followed by a fresh
    18	request before operation resumes.
    19	
    20	GOAL-01: The system shall publish one unambiguous commanded phase and mutually coherent
    21	power, charging, and flight permissions for every finite input and state combination.
    22	
    23	GOAL-02: The system shall distinguish valid low-battery awareness from invalid input and
    24	shall expose the distinction to the monitoring pilot without claiming physical battery
    25	performance.
    26	
    27	GOAL-03: The system shall prevent an invalid or previously sampled request from being
    28	replayed as an operational transition during recovery.
    29	
    30	GOAL-04: The system should remain small enough for complete case enumeration,
    31	responsibility audit, trace review, and human review without count-only usages or
    32	interactions.
    33	
    34	### Operational context and exact system boundary
    35	
    36	CTX-01: The Lifecycle Request Source is outside the system and supplies one request
    37	event plus its validity status per logical evaluation. The corpus does not name this
    38	source; introducing it is an explicit pilot abstraction and does not assign command
    39	authority to the pilot.
    40	
    41	CTX-02: The Battery Management Context is outside the system and supplies a qualitative
    42	capacity indication plus validity status. The abstract neither measures charge nor
    43	infers physical endurance.
    44	
    45	CTX-03: The Drone Lifecycle Enactor is outside the system and receives a logical
    46	enablement outcome. Receipt is observable at the boundary; physical execution or success
    47	is outside scope.
    48	
    49	CTX-04: The Pilot is outside the system and receives commanded-phase and attention
    50	reports for monitoring. The source supports the pilot's monitoring role only; no pilot
    51	command role is inferred.
    52	
    53	MON-01: `LifecycleRequestSample` is a finite root input from CTX-01 with fields `event :
    54	LifecycleEvent` and `status : InputStatus`. `LifecycleEvent` is exactly `{NoRequest,
    55	SwitchOn, SwitchOff, BeginCharge, EndCharge, Activate, Deactivate, BeginFlight,
    56	EndFlight}` and `InputStatus` is exactly `{Valid, Invalid}`.
    57	
    58	MON-02: `BatterySample` is a finite root input from CTX-02 with fields `indication :
    59	BatteryIndication` and `status : InputStatus`. `BatteryIndication` is exactly
    60	`{Adequate, Low}`; these labels are qualitative pilot abstractions with no numeric
    61	charge, endurance, or unit claim.
    62	
    63	CTRL-01: `LifecycleActuation` is a finite root output to CTX-03 with fields `power :
    64	PowerPermission`, `chargingPermitted : Boolean`, and `flightPermitted : Boolean`.
    65	`PowerPermission` is exactly `{Disabled, StandbyEnabled, OperationalEnabled}`. These are
    66	commanded logical permissions, not achieved physical states.
    67	
    68	CTRL-02: `CommandedPhaseReport` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly the
    69	`LifecyclePhase` values `{Off, Standby, Charging, Ready, Flying}` and reports the phase
    70	selected for the completed evaluation.
    71	
    72	CTRL-03: `AttentionStatus` is a root output to CTX-04 with exactly `{None, LowBattery,
    73	InputFault, RecoveryAwaitingNeutral}`. It reports the highest-priority current attention
    74	condition and does not assert a physical hazard classification.
    75	
    76	### Nominal, boundary, fault, and recovery behavior
    77	
    78	RISK-01: If an invalid request or battery report were treated as trustworthy, the
    79	governor could publish an unintended lifecycle permission. The consequence within this
    80	logical model is an incoherent or unjustified command, not an asserted physical accident
    81	or severity classification.
    82	
    83	### Essential environmental assumptions and constraints
    84	
    85	ASM-01: CTX-01 is responsible for presenting exactly one event/status pair per logical
    86	evaluation and for presenting `NoRequest` when no event is requested. This assumption is
    87	needed to define neutral recovery; it does not claim how an external sender detects
    88	edges or schedules samples.
    89	
    90	ASM-02: CTX-02 is responsible for pairing every qualitative indication with an explicit
    91	validity status. `Adequate` and `Low` are mutually exclusive finite labels supplied to
    92	the governor; the abstract does not define a numeric boundary or guarantee their
    93	physical accuracy.
    94	
    95	ASM-03: CTX-03 is responsible only for accepting CTRL-01 as a logical command interface.
    96	The governor receives no achievement feedback, so commanded phase shall never be
    97	described as achieved flight, completed charging, landing, or physical power state.
    98	
    99	ASM-04: CTX-04 is responsible only for receiving CTRL-02 and CTRL-03. Monitoring does
   100	not imply that the pilot originated requests or that any external actor acted on the
   101	report.

   194

   196

   198

   204	
   205	> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall produce a result for which if recovery required is true, then current phase is Off, selected phase is current phase, and phase report is selected phase.
   206	
   207	##### `CASE_01_INVALID_INPUT` — Conditional behavior
   208	
   209	> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is Invalid Request or battery assessment is Invalid Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when T is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when T is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when T is true.

   212

   216

   220	
   221	> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, and qualified request is Switch Off, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Off, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Off, phase report to Off, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.

   224

   228	
   229	> During contract evaluation for the compute phase, if qualified request is not Invalid Request, battery assessment is not Invalid Battery, the value of recovery required on entry is true exactly when F is true, the value of current phase on entry is Standby, qualified request is Begin Charge, and battery assessment is Low Battery, Lifecycle Decision Owner shall set current phase to Charging, recovery required to true exactly when F is true, selected phase to Charging, phase report to Charging, decision disposition input fault detected to true exactly when F is true, and decision disposition recovery pending to true exactly when F is true.
